chapter: Chicago memories and the road to the Navy
title: Staying in Chicago until the snow and sending home for fare
summary: As a boy Zutty drifted about Chicago until the first snow scared him and he wired home for the $25.65 fare, then joined the Navy the next summer.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Yes. Well how long did you stay in Chicago on this trip?
On this trip? Gee I must have stayed quite a while.
Yes. Ah I got to be a Chicago boy man.
Well what did you live on? I mean you came up on the train. What did you live on up there?
Oh, we lived with Lil Armstrong.
No I mean when you came up as a boy. The first time you came up to Chicago as a kid.

Oh! That's when I had to send home for money for mamma to send for me to come home. When I first saw the snow. That scared me to death. And it was $25.65 was the fare from Chicago to New Orleans. Yes. Because I was just hitting about in spots, you know. Like I got there that summer and lived in there until that winter, see when that snow fell. That was it. And that next summer I joined the navy.
